items.prompt: In a payment authorization system, a payment coordinator must authorize a charge. the customer must not be charged twice when the provider response is delayed The design review focuses on authorization models, ownership, rbac, and abac. constraints: the customer must not be charged twice when the provider response is delayed
Choose the mechanism that directly satisfies the stated contract before adding adjacent controls.
The primary decision is authorize the requested action against server-side resource ownership and policy context..
Keep the scenario provider-neutral and do not rely on a canonical product solution.

options.text: Authorize the requested action against server-side resource ownership and policy context. In this normal path for payment authorization, authentication identifies a principal; authorization decides whether that principal may perform this operation. The owner must also make an ambiguous provider outcome observable rather than silently passing it to another layer.
Choose the nearest familiar component and let each caller decide authorization models, ownership, rbac, and abac independently, without a shared owner or failure contract.
Add replication, caching, retries, or asynchronous buffering immediately, even though the scenario has not shown that mechanism is the limiting constraint.
Keep the happy path and treat an ambiguous provider outcome as an operational exception that the caller can resolve manually.
Select a named cloud or vendor product first and infer the workload, ownership, and guarantee from that product's defaults.

Details.errorCorrection: The distractors either make the boundary unowned, add unmeasured complexity, ignore recovery, or replace mechanism reasoning with provider trivia. Choose the mechanism that directly satisfies the stated contract before adding adjacent controls.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not reduce “Authorization models, ownership, RBAC, and ABAC” to terminology recall. Authentication is not authorization, encryption is not isolation, and client-side controls are not enforcement; define explicit trust boundaries. options.text: Authorize the requested action against server-side resource ownership and policy context. In this transfer case for inventory reservation, authentication identifies a principal; authorization decides whether that principal may perform this operation. The owner must also make a stale read before a competing reservation observable rather than silently passing it to another layer.
Choose the nearest familiar component and let each caller decide authorization models, ownership, rbac, and abac independently, without a shared owner or failure contract.
